title: Find and use your tools faster
summary: Find tools faster, prepare data in Quick Query, and try the improved HTML Template preview, Redis Cache, and Kafka workflows.
notes: Search has moved to the top of the sidebar; click it or press ⌘K.
Desktop connection status in the header opens controls for Oracle, Kafka, and Redis.
Quick Query generates one or many UUIDs and copies them when you select Generate.
Quick Query now lets you keep sheet audit users, use SYSTEM, or save a custom audit user.
HTML Template supports document tabs, VTL field extraction, and preview controls for width, VTL rendering, and background.
Redis Cache helps you find, save, inspect, and clear cache keys.
Kafka supports reusable Publish drafts, topic favorites, message search, and live listening.

slides.title: Prepare data in Quick Query
slides.body: Create UUIDs, import Oracle rows, and choose who appears in generated audit user fields.
bullets: Select UUID, choose a count, and select Generate; the result is copied to your clipboard.
On Desktop, select Import Oracle to run a query and bring its results into the data sheet.
In the data sheet, choose Off to use cell values, SYSTEM to override them, or Custom to save your own audit user with the pencil.

slides.title: Find and clear Redis cache keys
slides.body: Set up a Redis connection, search for keys, and save the ones you use often.
bullets: Enter the host, port, and password in Settings, then test the connection.
Search with a Redis wildcard such as *config* or words such as app config; spaces become wildcards.
Save keys for quick access later, and confirm before clearing a key or selected keys.

slides.title: Work across HTML templates
slides.body: Keep templates in tabs, extract VTL variables, and inspect the preview at different widths.
bullets: Create another document tab and extract VTL fields from the current template.
Choose a preview width or a custom width to see how the template fits.
Show VTL plainly or render it, and switch the preview to a white background when useful.

tips.title: Search from here
tips.body: Click search to find tools, pages, and saved Quick Query schemas.

tips.title: Manage connections in the header
tips.body: Click the Oracle status to open connection controls. You can also manage Kafka and Redis here.

tips.title: Generate ready-to-use UUIDs
tips.body: Click UUID to open the generator.

next.body: Choose a count, then click Generate. The UUIDs will be copied to your clipboard.

tips.title: Import from Oracle
tips.body: Open Import Oracle to see how a query can fill the data sheet. A desktop connection is needed to run it.

tips.title: Choose an audit user
tips.body: Try SYSTEM or Custom for generated audit user fields. The pencil lets you save a custom value.

tips.title: Find VTL fields
tips.body: Click Extract VTL Fields to inspect variables in the current template. If it has no VTL, the panel will say so.

tips.title: Keep templates in tabs
tips.body: Click New HTML document to open another editable tab.

tips.title: Check the preview width
tips.body: Choose a device width or Custom width to see how your HTML fits.

tips.title: Compare VTL preview modes
tips.body: Switch between rendered VTL and showing the VTL syntax plainly.

tips.title: Preview on white
tips.body: Click the background button to inspect transparent HTML against white.

tips.title: Set up Redis
tips.body: Open Settings to enter the Redis host, port, and password, then use Test connection.

tips.title: Find cache keys
tips.body: Search with *config* or type app config; spaces become wildcards. Save useful keys for quick access and clear them after confirmation.

tips.title: Reuse a Publish draft
tips.body: Favorite a topic, save a template for repeated publishing, and add an optional trace ID in Options > Headers.

tips.title: Search or listen live
tips.body: Choose a topic and search by trace ID, CIF, or payload from a chosen time; switch to Live for new messages.
